We tried the Rasam Wada, which was delicious — the rasam was served hot and perfectly spicy! The idlis were soft, and the sambar was very tasty. Along with the regular coconut chutney, they also serve 4 different chutneys, all of which were really good.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: RAHUL V
featured_reviews.review_text:
So i visited madras diaries which is located in bandra west i must say

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Dethe
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a lovely experience at Madras Diaries. The food was authentic, flavorful, and reminded me of true South Indian taste. The ambience was cozy and the service was quick and friendly. Definitely a great spot for a satisfying meal!

featured_reviews.name: Narendra Bhuwalka
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries Bandra West now serves South Indian classics with a new chaat menu that is already a hit
You get tangy crunchy plates like pani puri and bhel along with crispy dosas idlis rasam shots and filter coffee
The drinks are refreshing and pair well with the bold flavorful and addictive chaat

If you want variety great taste and an ambiance that lifts your mood this is the perfect comfort food fix with a chatpata twist

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Ashford
featured_reviews.review_text: I thoroughly enjoyed the Mysore Masala Dosa, Idli Vada, Mini Idli, Pineapple Sheera, and Filter Coffee. Every item was delightful. Food took a while to be served, but it was fine for us. Highly recommended.

customer_updates.name: Yogesh Sharma
customer_updates.text:
South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

While our experience, the food, and the service were great, what surprised me was a South Indian restaurant whose Sambar was so average. That being said, multiple visits to The Tanjore Tiffin Room are in my future.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prettily lit entrance leading a climb of a couple of floors to the restaurant (there is a lift). At 7:30 pm, several tables were already occupied.

Nicely presented menus, friendly staff, delicious home style recipes served in chunky brass dishes, complementary colours and textures.

Small tasting bowls of curry and rice samples are a prelude to the main course. The food is heavy, so go easy on the ordering!

We had hardly finished our starters, when the main courses piled up on the table...service could be staggered slightly.

Loos are off a small landing and could be cleaner. On our way out, the entrance area had become jammed with waiting guests, a tight situation, as were the takeaway boxes, which were over-stuffed.

featured_reviews.name: Daniel Harrington
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely stunning in every way.

Fell across this place via Google maps and waited until 10pm for a table (our fault we didn't book), however it did not disappoint.

Genuinely a top 5 all time restaurant for me. The food, the service, the ambience absolutely top tier. I have never had Indian food (from any region) as flavourful. The staff explained the concept and dishes incredibly well and the taster platter to help decide what to order was so fantastic. I would recommend this to absolutely everyone who lives in or is visiting Mumbai.

Thanks for an unforgettable night.

Please open up in London!!

Best Dessert: The Almond Halwa is exceptional.

Convenience: Great Jain options.

Vibe: Very cozy and authentic (small seating capacity, so be ready to wait).

featured_reviews.name: Yash Bagal

I visited Benne - Heritage Bangalore Dosa Overall Experience was great.This is one of the best South Indian restaurants I have tried especially for dosa and idli lovers.

Very crispy and full of flavour. This was the best dosa I have ever tried. Highly recommended.

Extremely delicious and rich in taste. One of the best Thatte Idlis I have ever eaten. Must try.

4. Akki Roti:
Taste was okay, nothing special. Not recommended compared to other items.

5. Donne Pulav:
Pulav was okay, but the raita was very tasty and made the dish better.

👉Tips:
The restaurant closes at 3:30 PM and reopens at 5:30 PM. They also provide umbrellas during strong sunlight, which is helpful.

👉Suggestion:
It would be better if cold drinking water was provided.

featured_reviews.name: Jay Velwan

I recently visited Benne Dosa Place and really enjoyed the food. I tried the Ghee Podi Masala Dosa and Garlic Podi Masala Dosa, and both were very flavorful and delicious. I also had the Ghee Podi Thatte Idli, which was the highlight of my visit — it was soft, tasty, and absolutely amazing.
Their red chutney was the real star of the meal. It paired perfectly with both the dosa and idli and tasted incredible.
I also tried the filter coffee, which was just average compared to how good the food was.
One downside is that the place is quite small. It gets crowded, and it can be difficult to stand and collect orders comfortably. The AC also didn’t seem to be working, which made it a bit uncomfortable.

Overall, the food quality is excellent, especially the Thatte Idli and red chutney, and I would definitely recommend trying them.

featured_reviews.name: Prabhjit Singh Modi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dosa and Thatte Idli both of them were good. What they could really add to the menu is some basic empathy.

I came from Vadodara after a 6-hour train journey and reached around 5:45 am. This was the first place I walked into straight from the railway station. At 6:00 am I politely asked the manager, the one with specs, if I could just sit in the corner since the space was empty and their setup was done. He flatly refused and said I could only enter at 7:00 am.

My back was hurting after the journey and I just needed a place to sit for a bit. It wouldn’t have cost them anything to show a little understanding. Instead, it was a straight no, no conversation.

If this were a smaller outlet, I’m pretty sure someone would’ve just said, “Haan bhai, sit.” Instead, he just didn’t allow it. No explanation, no actual rule, just a straight no. The place was empty, I wasn’t asking for free food, just a corner for 60 minutes after a 6-hour train ride. It honestly felt unnecessary and ego-driven.

That’s what happens when brands get big. A little success and suddenly basic decency becomes optional and Money gets to their head.

Massive respect though to the slim guy who seemed like the asst manager. He kept asking if I wanted to sit on his bike outside. That genuinely melted my heart. At least someone there understood basic humanity.

Food is good. The attitude needs serious work.

Even their chutneys are really good and pair perfectly with the dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Vinay Pasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mutuswami Cafe in Khar and really enjoyed the overall experience. The place has a simple, casual vibe but serves a wide variety of dishes—from authentic South Indian options to Mumbai street-style favourites.

The benne dosa stood out with its crispy texture and buttery flavour, while the idli was soft and fresh. The cheese pav bhaji and mushroom sukha combo added a nice desi touch to the meal. The mango milkshake and mango sheera were rich, sweet, and perfect to end on a high note.

Service was quick, though it can get a bit crowded during peak hours. Overall, it’s a great place for breakfast or a casual meal with good food and decent pricing. Would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: sourabh debnath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at muttuswami Khar🌟
Started with the refreshing Kala Khatta and Aam Panna coolers — both were perfect for the Mumbai heat. The Ghee Podi Idli was super soft and flavourful, while the Masala Benne Dosa was buttery, crisp and delicious. For mains, the Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam and Chettinad Biryani were packed with authentic flavours and tasted amazing. Ended the meal with Payasam and Vanilla Gelato which made for the perfect dessert combo. Great food, comforting flavours and an overall amazing dining experience. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mahima Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Khar outlet recently and absolutely loved the whole experience 🫶🏻

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

featured_reviews.name: Komal Jaisingh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami is one of those simple, comforting south indian food places which serve superb food. Calm and relaxed vibe - no rush, no noise just pure happiness. We absolutely loved the Paper masala Dosa, and podi idli.. two of my favs here. Apart from that they also serve Grilled Sandwiches, Pav Bhaji and an amazing line up of dosas and juices.
Had to end our meal with the super amazing Pineapple Sheera and filter coffee !! Manawwar served us really well !

featured_reviews.name: harshad lagade

featured_reviews.name: FJT
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Muttuswami Café with my skeptical, firang partner. He loved it, and so did I.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

I only dock one star because the AC wasn't working, and it's upwards of 35 degrees C right now. But honestly, the food was worth it.

10/10, would recommend!

The decor and overall aesthetic of this place are truly beautiful. The ambiance, design, and attention to detail make it feel like a high-end spot, and walking in, you definitely expect a premium dining experience. Unfortunately, while the space looks stunning, the actual experience did not live up to the expectations, especially considering the reputation and standard one would associate with a place like this.

The biggest issue by far was the number of bugs. There were so many insects flying around our table while we were eating, which completely ruined the experience. What made it even more uncomfortable was that the staff were actively killing bugs right next to us as we were dining, which felt extremely unhygienic and honestly quite disgusting. It completely took away from the enjoyment of the meal and made it hard to relax or even finish our food comfortably. For a restaurant of this level, this is simply unacceptable and needs serious attention.

In terms of the food, it was a mixed experience. The watermelon and pineapple juices were good — fresh, refreshing, and nicely prepared. The watermelon salad, however, lacked flavor and felt quite underwhelming, especially given how promising it sounded on the menu.

We ordered the edamame peas and the spicy chicken, and those dishes were actually quite good. They were well-cooked, flavorful, and enjoyable, which showed that the kitchen does have potential. However, good dishes alone cannot make up for poor hygiene standards and an uncomfortable dining environment.

The service also felt below expectation. It didn’t reflect the quality, attentiveness, or polish you would normally associate with a Bastian-level standard. Overall, the experience felt disorganized and lacking in the fine-dining attention to detail that one would expect.

In summary, while the decor is stunning and some of the food items were good, the bug issue and service quality seriously impacted the experience. It did not feel like a Bastian-standard restaurant, and until these issues are resolved, it’s hard to recommend. With better hygiene control, improved service, and more consistency in food quality, this place could truly live up to its potential — but for now, it unfortunately falls short.

A small bowl full of plain cooked rice. Quality of the rice was good and it went really well with all the above dishes.

I’d recommend people ordering food from here to have Chicken Chetinad, Mangalorean Chicken, Steamed Rice and Papad.

If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at Hoppumm, a cozy Sri Lankan restaurant tucked away in Khar West.

The moment we stepped in, we were greeted with a warm and lively ambiance – minimalist yet vibrant decor that instantly transported us to the streets of Shrilanka.

Ambiance and Setting:
The interiors are stylish yet casual, perfect for a relaxed evening. Beautifully painted walls, masks hanged on the wall and subtle lighting created an inviting atmosphere.

Service:
The service was quick, efficient, and polite. Special thanks to Mr. Imran for his wonderful hospitality — he patiently introduced us to the different dishes and ensured prompt service throughout the evening, making our experience even more memorable.

Food Quality:
We tried a variety of dishes:

Pineapple & Basil Cooler (refreshing and balanced)

Kokum Sharbat (perfectly tangy and cooling)

Chicken & Cheese Kottu (a hearty, flavorful dish and is a MUST TRY)

Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken (rich coconut broth with tender chicken)

Green Mango Chicken Curry (tangy, creamy curry served in a portion fit for one person)

Traditional Hopper (light and crispy, served along with Podi)

Hot Butter Squid (crispy yet juicy with a burst of flavors)

Lemony Chicken Delight Combo (the showstopper with a perfect balance of zest and spice. There were many different dishes added to rice including a fried chicken leg piece)

They also offered three different types of chatneys from spicy to sweet flavour and you can add according to your need.
Food wasn't much spicy.

Each dish was authentic, beautifully presented, and packed with bold flavors true to Sri Lankan cuisine. Portion sizes were quite satisfying for the price.

Hoppumm is a hidden gem for those looking to explore Sri Lankan cuisine in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Hoppum, a true haven for authentic Sri Lankan cuisine, and it was quite the culinary journey!

We began with the Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken, where tender chicken was stuffed into green chillies — a brilliant fusion of juicy meat, aromatic spices, and bold chilli heat. It set the tone for what we hoped would be an exciting meal.

The Chicken and Cheese Kottu followed, a popular Sri Lankan street dish featuring finely chopped roti tossed with vegetables and chicken. It was delicious, evoking nostalgic Indian chaat vibes (think ragda pattice) with its hearty and comforting flavors.

The Green Mango Chicken Curry was a standout — silky smooth, subtly tangy with green mango, and enriched with coconut. Paired with their traditional Hopper (similar to an appam), it was an absolute treat.

We also tried the Hot Butter Squid, which was flavorful and perfectly chewy — a must for seafood enthusiasts.

Portion sizes for starters felt on the smaller side, especially considering the price point. Another important thing to note was the food was pre-prepared, and simply heated and served.

To beat the heat, the bottled Pineapple & Basil Cooler and Kokum Sherbet provided much-needed refreshment.

Our meal wrapped up with the Lemony Chicken Delight Combo Rice, served beautifully in a banana leaf with rice, chicken leg, coconut chutneys, and garnishes. Unfortunately, while visually appealing, it lacked the bold flavors we anticipated and felt a bit bland.

While the restaurant greets you with a pleasant, warm ambiance, the seating feels quite congested. The small tables and pocket-café vibe were a bit of a letdown, especially for a place that serves such vibrant cuisine.

The Kerala Parotha was also quite good. The filter coffee was also authentic with a choice of sugar-free as well. Perhaps the biggest negative is the limited choice of main course dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Alessandro Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good place for some South Indian food.
Recommendations : Masala Dosa, Veg Chettinad, tamarind rice, lemon rice, bisi belle bhat and Payasam.
They have appams too, however not worth it for the price, can be skipped.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
UPPU – A South Indian Kitchen in Bandra West is truly one of those rare places that gets everything right. I happened to visit UPPU in the last week of January 2026. From the moment you step in, the ambience immediately sets the tone. It’s warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — giving you a sense of comfort that makes you want to sit back and enjoy your meal without any rush. The interiors have a subtle South Indian touch, yet feel modern and elegant at the same time.

The food is where UPPU really shines. The taste is genuinely authentic — you can tell that attention has been paid to traditional recipes and flavours. Every dish feels carefully prepared, balanced, and true to its roots. The spices are not overpowering, the flavours are layered, and the overall experience feels wholesome rather than heavy. It’s the kind of place where you don’t just eat, you savour.

Another thing that stood out for me was the service. The staff is extremely well mannered, polite, and attentive. What I particularly appreciated is that they are present when needed but never intrusive. They don’t interrupt your dining or conversations unnecessarily, which makes the overall experience even more pleasant. It’s rare to find that perfect balance of attentiveness without interference.

Despite being located in Bandra West, where restaurants are plenty and competition is high, UPPU manages to create its own identity. It feels premium yet comfortable, refined yet relaxed. Whether you’re visiting for a family dinner, a quiet catch-up with friends, or even a business conversation, the setting works beautifully.

UPPU is a wonderful South Indian Restaurant and is definitely a place I would visit again and highly recommend to anyone looking for quality dining in Bandra West.

featured_reviews.name: 1TeaspoonLove
featured_reviews.review_text:
Uppu is a quint, cozy yet elegant place at Bandra reclamation serving authentic South Indian food.

They have a small menu but covers all the classics.

We began with a refreshing cold filter coffee followed by ghee podi idli. The idlis could have been softer and fluffier. They were a little dry.

Benne dosa and Mysore masala dosa. Both were crisp and good.

Mushroom ghee roast.. tasted okay.

The food was very heavy. I could barely eat.
It was a hit & miss for me.

We ended with a filter coffee and sheera. Both were good.

Overall decent food.

featured_reviews.name: sapana chhaparwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been wanting to try this place for quite some time now but turned out really disappointing.
Positives - Thuppa dosa and thuppa idli was outstanding. Filter Coffee had bit caramelised flavor but nice. Rasam was perfectly tangy, spicy and right consistency…

However - what’s making be give 2 stars is the “SWEETNESS” in Benne an onion rava dosa!!! Like who on earth adds sweetness to these dishes?? Rava dosa wasn’t even so much of rava but something else altogether

Guys, I don’t know what got that sweetness to those dishes but please don’t ruin them

featured_reviews.name: Harsh S. Moorjani
featured_reviews.review_text:
5/5 – An absolute gem that deserves far more recognition (Highly recommended)

Uppu serves exceptional South Indian fare, the dosas are perfectly crisp, the idlis are soft and fluffy, and every dish is prepared with care. The flavours are authentic and consistently excellent.

What sets this place apart is the warmth, the staff is genuinely courteous, the service is efficient, and the interiors are cozy without trying too hard. It’s the kind of neighbourhood spot that feels welcoming from the moment you walk in.

For those who queue endlessly at Benne, consider this your insider tip. Uppu is nearby, less crowded, and frankly, just as good, if not better. It’s close to home for me, which means I’ve been here enough times to know that this place deserves the footfall it hasn’t yet received.

featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful interior with good ambiance. They have musical nights as Thursday seems Karaoke night. Lots of people to sing. Food is not bad but average. Service is not bad too. Very attentive servers. Street parking only.

featured_reviews.name: Merlyn
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had originally checked with Soul Fry for their karaoke nights, but the owner mentioned that reservations usually need to be made around 10 days to 2 weeks in advance. Later, we ended up going there for lunch on one of the days. I had even called beforehand to ask if reservations were necessary, and he said yes, definitely. But when we actually reached, the restaurant was pretty empty.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwinth Naveen
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in Mumbai, and I have absolutely no regrets choosing Soul Fry as my go-to spot! The karaoke night was an absolute blast and made the whole experience even more memorable. The vibe, music, and overall atmosphere were amazing, and I genuinely had such a great time. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip — would love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Marlyn Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re into authentic Goan food this is a great place to be. They have karaoke in the evenings and is usually packed so you might have to book in advance, or take only outside seating. The bombil fry and pompfret rechado is a must try.

featured_reviews.name: DS
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of my favourite places in Mumbai. They have karaoke nights and also other events happening everyday. When we visited, there was a live music and karaoke night happening. They have a nice variety of cocktails and liquor available. We also tried their prawn rava fry and it was absolutely superb.

It does get extremely crowded on the weekends so getting a table will be difficult. But they let you stand around and order and also have free peanuts. Nice place for seafood.
